note: Read by smart search at startup; smart-search/readme says what every field means and how to tune them.

question.note: Score rather than Noul: better at most levels in the first measurement, since the tiers say what kind of match to look for. The same criteria everywhere until tuning says a level wants its own.
criteria: no relevance to the query topic
question.text: `{level}` is the {what} of one stored document. Is that document likely to be relevant to the search query `query`?

levels.name: title
levels.note: Supporting only: a title labels rather than describes, so a generic one gets a low answer, and counted against it ruled out the best document for a query.

levels.name: keywords
levels.note: Beside the title, being as short and written for the same purpose, and supporting only for the same reason.

levels.name: summary
levels.note: Before contents: shorter, and says what a document is for rather than what is in it.

levels.name: body
levels.what: text, or one part of it,

scoring.note: A starting point, not a result: measuring against labelled queries is what sets these.

requests.note: chunk_chars: Jev takes 32k tokens for the state and the longest question together, at near four characters a token, less room for the question and for text that tokenises badly.
